questiontext.text:
We have simulated data sets giving the crop yield for different crops. The outcome variable is the Crop Yield, and the explanatory variables are:

  • Soil Quality Index Score - a numerical variable ranging from 1-10, representing soil quality, where higher scores indicate better quality.
  • Crop Planted - a factor variable indicating the type of crop planted.
  • Region - a factor variable specifying the region (North or South).
  • Density of pests in the crop - a numerical variable indicating the density of pests in the crop.
  • Pest susceptibility - a factor variable with three levels (low, medium, high) representing how susceptible the given crop is to pests.

The following visualisation shows the crop yield on the Y axis and the Soil Quality Index Score on the X axis. There are then dimensions built up from “aesthetics”.

Here, we have the colour as the crop type. There are two panels: The left displays for the North regions, and the right for the South regions.

In this plot, we can see that the Soil Quality Index Score is correlated to the crop yield in the South region. As the Soil Quality Index Score increases in the South region, the yield increases. In the North region, it is unclear whether the Soil Quality Index Score is correlated to the crop yield. All three crops perform similarly to one another between the two regions.

There does not seem to be a difference in the yield between the three crops in either region. There are some fluctuations but due to a small amount of data it is unclear.

Download this data. This is not the same as the data used to make the graphic above. Using the downloaded data, create a similar visualisation.

Which of the following statement(s) are true. Check all that apply:

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

questionvariables.text: ta: random_permutation([[1, false, "The Crop Yield is not affected by the Region"], [2, false, "The Crop Yield is not affected by the Crop Type"], [3, true, "In the North Region, the Sorghum crop tends to result in the highest yield of the three crops"], [4, true, "In the North Region, the Soil Quality Index Score is always correlated with the Crop Yield regardless of Crop"], [5, true, "In the South Region, the Corn and Rice crop tend to result in the highest yield"], [6, true, "Corn and Rice are impacted the same way as the region moves from North to South"], [7, true, "The Soil Quality Index Score is not correlated with the Crop Yield for Sorghum in the South Region"]]);

truefeedback.text:
You selected "In the North Region, the Sorghum crop tends to result in the highest yield of the three crops", which is correct. If we look at the North Region only, we can see that the Sorghum crop tends to consistently result in the highest yield.

You selected "In the North Region, the Soil Quality Index Score is always correlated with the Crop Yield regardless of Crop", which is correct. If we look at the North Region only, we can see that the yield increases as the Soil Quality Index Score increases for all crops (although only a small amount for the Corn and Rice crops).

You selected "In the South Region, the Corn and Rice crop tend to result in the highest yield", which is correct. If we look at the South Region only, we can see that the Corn and Rice crops tend to consistently result in the highest yield.

You selected "Corn and Rice are impacted the same way as the region moves from North to South", which is correct. This one is a tricky one, so well done! The difference between corn and rice is the same in both panels for the North and South regions. This means that both Corn and Rice are impacted the same way as the region moves from North to South.

You selected "The Soil Quality Index Score is not correlated with the Crop Yield for Sorghum in the South Region", which is correct. For Sorghum in the South Region, there seems to be no change in the yield as the Soil Quality Index Score increases.
